# Product requirements

## Repository template requirements

### Purpose

Provide a minimal, technology-neutral GitHub repository template for work coordinated by humans and software agents. The template itself is infrastructure, not an application.

### Canonical workspace

- Keep `GOAL.md`, generated `PRD.md`, generated `ARCHITECTURE.md`, generated `AGENTS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TODO.md` and `SCRATCHPAD.md` at the top of `.darkfactory/agents/` (also accessible through the root `.agents` symlink).
- Keep small working notes under `.darkfactory/agents/notes/`, approved requirements under `.darkfactory/agents/requests/`, accepted architectural decisions under `.darkfactory/agents/decisions/` and active rules under `.darkfactory/agents/rules/`.
- Keep reusable role descriptions in `.darkfactory/agents/agents/` and executable, runtime-agnostic guidance in `.darkfactory/agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. A role is not a duplicate ruleset; a skill is a procedure, not automatically installed code.
- Generate `.darkfactory/agents/README.md` from published records in `.darkfactory/agents/notes/`, `.darkfactory/agents/PRD.md` from approved requests, `.darkfactory/agents/ARCHITECTURE.md` from accepted decisions, and `.darkfactory/agents/AGENTS.md` from active rules. Generated documents must never be edited as independent sources.
- Root `README.md` must be a Git symlink to `.agents/README.md`; root `CONTRIBUTING.md` must remain a Git symlink to `.agents/AGENTS.md`.
- Keep `.darkfactory/agents/TODO.md` as the non-generated task worklist; it is not a README source.

- Store the former `.github` tree in `.darkfactory/github/`, the former `.agents` tree in `.darkfactory/agents/`, and make `.github` and `.agents` real Git symlinks to those folders.
- Require every repository test (unit, integration, end-to-end, fixtures, snapshots and test helpers) to live somewhere below `.darkfactory/tests/`; do not create competing test directories.
- Keep GitHub Actions workflows in the consolidated tree, but do not claim that GitHub discovers workflows through the `.github` symlink without live proof. If undiscoverable, automated checks, version bumps and releases remain unavailable until a supported activation arrangement is approved.

### Delivery

- Keep a machine-readable `VERSION` file and combined `repo.dfconfig` at root.
- Use a persistent `development` integration branch. Permit pull requests into `main` only when their source is the same repository's `development` branch.
- Bump the version once for each same-repository pull request, and tag and publish a GitHub Release after a change lands on `main`.
- Declare branch-protection policy, enforce review and checks when administrative access permits, and verify the live GitHub state rather than claiming a config file is enforcement.
- License the template under GPL-3.0.
- Do not install language-specific build tooling or pretend an empty template has application tests.
